predecessors.name: New France
predecessors.text: the Saint Lawrence valley of Quebec: the colony of 1763, which 'did not extend as far west as the Great Lakes or as far north as Rupert's Land'

successors.name: Upper Canada
successors.text: southern Ontario, the north shore of the Great Lakes

successors.name: Lower Canada
successors.text: the Saint Lawrence valley and the Labrador coast

ledger.x: 1763: the Province of Quebec is created.
1774: the Labrador coast passes from Newfoundland to Quebec.
1774: the Quebec Act enlarges the province.
1783: the lands south of the Great Lakes pass to the United States.
1791: the colony is divided at the Ottawa River.
1791: Lower Canada, the eastern part on the Saint Lawrence, is created by the Constitutional Act (26 December 1791).
1791: the Province of Quebec ends on 26 December 1791 with the Constitutional Act.

certainty.note: The Proclamation named the colony's limits only in the negative (not to the Great Lakes, not to Rupert's Land).
The Quebec Act boundaries ran to the Mississippi and the Ohio but were not surveyed.
The 1783 line through the Great Lakes was not fixed on the ground until the Jay Treaty of 1795 (Upper Canada page).
